design.title: StackSmith + docubot — Product Presentation
design.reference: Grafana dashboard / terminal / Vercel dark deck

slides.title: Cover — StackSmith + docubot
slides.task_brief:
COVER SLIDE. Full-bleed dark background (var(--bg)) with the optional .grid-bg overlay for an ops-console feel. Top-left: a small monospace tag 'v1.1.4 · stable' in var(--accent). Center-left block:
- Eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim), uppercase, letter-spaced): 'PRODUCT PRESENTATION'
- Main title (Space Grotesk, ~64px, var(--text)): 'StackSmith + docubot'
- Subtitle (Space Grotesk medium, ~28px, var(--primary)): 'Self-hosted document chat, production-grade operability.'
- One-line descriptor (Inter, ~17px, var(--text-dim)): 'A single VPS. No Kubernetes. No cloud lock-in. MIT-licensed.'
Bottom-left footer (monospace micro, var(--text-mute)): 'github.com/Abolfazlrwm/stacksmith   ·   release v1.1.4   ·   2026'
Bottom-right: a compact stack of three monospace stat chips arranged horizontally: '29 ADRs', '27 CI workflows', '16 releases'. Each chip is a small rounded card (var(--bg-card)) with the number in var(--accent) and the label below in var(--text-dim). No photos. No icons except optionally a single Material Icon 'bolt' in var(--accent) before the title. Layout must be balanced, generous whitespace, NOT cramped.
Speaker notes: Open by framing the two bad options (SaaS data leak vs becoming an SRE); docubot is the middle ground; this deck shows both the product and what makes it operable.

slides.title: The problem — two bad options
slides.task_brief:
PROBLEM SLIDE. Header at top: eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'THE PROBLEM' and H1 (Space Grotesk, ~44px, var(--text)) 'Teams want a chat assistant over private documents. They get two bad options.'
Below the header, TWO equal-width comparison cards side by side (use .card), each ~540px wide:

CARD 1 — header row with a warn-dot (red/amber) and title (Space Grotesk 24px) '1.  A SaaS chat product'. Body (Inter 17px): 'Convenient, but you must upload every document to a third party. A non-starter for legal, medical, financial, or any sensitive corpus.' Below body, a small monospace tag in var(--danger): 'data leaves your machine'.

CARD 2 — header row with a warn-dot and title '2.  Self-host an open-source model'. Body: 'No data leaves, but now you are an SRE. TLS, backups, deploys, monitoring, alerting, disaster recovery — before the product is usable. Most teams underestimate this by an order of magnitude.' Tag in var(--danger): 'you become a part-time ops team'.

Between / below the two cards, centered, an accent line and the question (Space Grotesk 28px, var(--primary)): 'There is no middle ground today.' Then below in var(--text-dim) 17px: 'Either your data leaves, or you become an operations team.'
Footer micro: '02 / 11'.
No images. Use Material Icons 'cloud_off' (card 1) and 'build' (card 2) in var(--text-mute) next to the card titles.
Speaker notes: The two options are bad for opposite reasons; this slide sets up docubot as the middle ground.

slides.title: The product — docubot
slides.task_brief:
PRODUCT SLIDE. Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'THE PRODUCT'. H1 (Space Grotesk 44px, var(--text)): 'docubot — the middle ground.'
Lead paragraph (Inter 18px, var(--text), max-width ~960px): 'Upload PDFs, Markdown, and plain-text documents, then ask questions of them in a chat interface. Answers are grounded in your own documents via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over a pgvector index — the model cites the source passage for each answer.'

Below, a 3×2 bento grid of six feature cards (each .card, ~360×140px). Each card: a Material Icon (var(--primary)) top-left, a bold short title (Space Grotesk 18px), and a one-line description (Inter 14px, var(--text-dim)).
1. icon 'forum' — 'Document chat' — 'Natural-language Q&A; answers cite source passages.'
2. icon 'manage_search' — 'RAG over pgvector' — 'Postgres-native vector storage. No separate vector DB.'
3. icon 'description' — 'Multi-format ingestion' — 'PDF, Markdown, plain text.'
4. icon 'shield' — 'Self-hosted' — 'Documents never leave your machine.'
5. icon 'group' — 'Multi-user' — 'Per-user collections and chat history.'
6. icon 'tune' — 'Model-agnostic' — 'OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local model.'
Footer micro: '03 / 11'.
Speaker notes: Stress that the only outbound call is the LLM completion; documents stay on-host; pgvector avoids a separate vector DB to run and back up.

slides.title: StackSmith — the operability layer
slides.task_brief:
OPERABILITY SLIDE. Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'THE DEPLOYMENT KIT'. H1 (Space Grotesk 44px, var(--text)): 'StackSmith — production-grade operability on one VPS.'
Lead (Inter 17px, var(--text-dim), max-width ~960px): 'The deployment kit that makes docubot operable: nginx, Postgres, Redis, full observability, encrypted backups, blue-green deploys, signed images, SLOs, runbooks. No Kubernetes, no cloud lock-in, no per-seat fees.'

Below, a two-column list of 8 capability rows (each row: a green check-dot '·' or Material Icon 'check_circle' in var(--ok), a bold capability name (Space Grotesk 16px), and a one-line proof (Inter 14px, var(--text-dim)). Two columns of 4 rows each:
Left column:
- Zero-downtime deploy — blue/green + canary + auto-rollback
- Encrypted backups — pg_dump → age → off-host; restore drill
- Disaster recovery — total VPS loss → restore → verify (CI)
- Full observability — metrics, logs, traces, alerts, 6 dashboards
Right column:
- SLOs + error budget — 99.5% availability, latency, 5xx (ADR-0033)
- Supply-chain security — multi-arch, cosign sign + verify, SBOM
- TLS automation — certbot renewal loop
- Secret rotation — zero-downtime rotation drill (ADR-0013)
Footer micro: '04 / 11'.
Speaker notes: Most self-hosted LLM projects stop at a docker-compose + README; StackSmith ships the operability layer those projects assume someone else builds.

slides.title: Architecture at a glance
slides.task_brief:
ARCHITECTURE SLIDE — render the topology as nested rounded cards/boxes using HTML+CSS ONLY (no SVG, no connector lines drawn in code; use CSS grid + borders to imply grouping). Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'ARCHITECTURE'. H1 (Space Grotesk 36px, var(--text)) 'One VPS. Eleven containers.'

Build the layout as a labeled layered diagram using stacked horizontal bands (each band a full-width .card-elev with a small monospace band label on the left):

BAND A — label 'EDGE': one wide card 'nginx' (Material Icon 'dns', subtitle 'reverse proxy · TLS · maintenance mode · rate limit').
BAND B — label 'APP': three cards in a row — 'app-blue' (icon 'play_arrow'), 'app-green' (icon 'play_arrow', var(--ok)), 'worker / beat' (icon 'schedule'). Subtitle under app-blue/green: 'Django · blue-green zero-downtime'.
BAND C — label 'DATA': two cards — 'postgres' (icon 'storage', subtitle 'Postgres 17 + pgvector') and 'redis' (icon 'memory', subtitle 'Celery broker + cache').
BAND D — label 'OBSERVABILITY': five small cards in a row — 'prometheus', 'loki', 'tempo', 'alertmanager', 'grafana' (each icon 'analytics' or similar, monospace label).

Below the bands, a single accent line and a footnote (Inter 14px, var(--text-dim)): 'Backups: pg_dump → age encryption → off-host copy. Supply chain: multi-arch GHCR + cosign keyless signing.'
Footer micro: '05 / 11'.
Keep all text legible; cards must not overflow the 1280×720 canvas. Use monospace for container names.
Speaker notes: Walk the bands top-to-bottom; emphasize pgvector lives inside Postgres (no separate vector DB); the observability stack is the same one Grafana itself ships.

slides.title: SLOs — the contract
slides.task_brief:
SLO SLIDE. Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'SERVICE LEVEL OBJECTIVES'. H1 (Space Grotesk 44px, var(--text)) 'Three SLOs. Every one wired to an alert.'

Main content: a clean 4-column table/grid with header row (monospace, var(--text-mute), uppercase, 12px): SLO | TARGET | WINDOW | ALERT.
Three data rows (each a .card row, ~110px tall, generous padding):
1. Availability — '99.5%' (huge, var(--primary), JetBrains Mono 40px) — '30 days' — alert chip 'SLOAvailabilityDown' (var(--danger), label 'critical · fast-burn')
2. Latency P99 — '< 500 ms' (var(--primary), 40px) — '5 minutes' — alert chip 'SLOLatencyP99Breach' (var(--warn), 'warning')
3. 5xx quality — '< 2% ratio' (var(--primary), 40px) — '5 minutes' — alert chip 'SLOHigh5xxRate' (var(--danger), 'critical · fast-burn')

Below the table, a callout band (var(--bg-elev), rounded): a Material Icon 'pie_chart' in var(--accent), then text (Inter 16px): 'The 30-day error budget at 99.5% is ~3.6 hours of allowed downtime per month. Both fast-burn (2-min) and slow-burn (30-day exhausted) alerts route to Alertmanager with severity routing.'
Footer micro: '06 / 11 · ADR-0033 · ADR-0035'.
Speaker notes: A deploy that returns 5xx for 30% of requests but keeps the health endpoint green will trip SLOHigh5xxRate — it would have slipped past an outage-only alert.

slides.title: Proven in CI — 27 workflows
slides.task_brief:
CI DRILLS SLIDE. Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'PROVEN IN CI'. H1 (Space Grotesk 40px, var(--text)) 'Not slides. Drills that run on every push.'
A big monospace stat at top-right: '27' (JetBrains Mono 56px, var(--accent)) with label below (var(--text-dim) 14px) 'CI workflows'.

Below, a 3×3 bento grid (9 cards, each .card ~340×120px) of the most important drills. Each card: a small monospace workflow-name top-left (var(--primary)), a one-line description (Inter 14px, var(--text-dim)) below. Use Material Icons in var(--text-mute) before each name.
1. 'deploy.yml' · icon 'sync' — 'blue→green→blue + canary probes'
2. 'canary-failure' · icon 'error_outline' — 'break green → auto-rollback'
3. 'restore-drill.yml' · icon 'restore' — 'backup → wipe → restore → verify'
4. 'encryption-drill' · icon 'lock' — 'encrypt → restore from .age → verify'
5. 'disaster-recovery-drill' · icon 'dangerous' — 'total VPS loss → encrypted restore → verify'
6. 'latency-sli-drill' · icon 'speed' — 'nginx log → promtail → prometheus → alerts'
7. 'slo-metrics-drill' · icon 'monitor_heart' — 'nginx-exporter up · availability SLI · alerts loaded'
8. 'chaos-drill' · icon 'bolt' — 'kill worker + stop nginx → recover'
9. 'k6 load test' · icon 'speed' — '50 VUs · p95 < 500ms'
Footer micro: '07 / 11'.
Speaker notes: The DR drill destroys the stack on a CI runner and rebuilds from an encrypted backup — if it passes, the DR story is a tested procedure, not a slide.

slides.title: Live demo — what we will show
slides.task_brief:
DEMO AGENDA SLIDE. Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'LIVE DEMO · ~15 MIN'. H1 (Space Grotesk 40px, var(--text)) 'Five beats. One VPS. Zero downtime.'

Main content: a vertical or horizontal step list of 5 numbered steps. Each step: a large monospace number (JetBrains Mono 40px, var(--accent)) like '01', a bold step title (Space Grotesk 22px, var(--text)), and a one-line detail (Inter 15px, var(--text-dim)). Arrange as 5 cards in a row (each ~220px wide, .card) OR as a horizontal timeline of 5 connected pills — either is fine, do NOT draw SVG connectors; use CSS borders/spacing to imply sequence.

01 — 'Document chat' — 'Ask a question across uploaded PDFs; answer cites sources.'
02 — 'Zero-downtime deploy' — 'deploy.sh green → canary probes → upstream switch.'
03 — 'CI drills' — 'The deploy + DR + latency drills that prove operability.'
04 — 'Observability + SLOs' — 'Grafana SLO dashboard; error-budget; alert routing.'
05 — 'Backup & restore' — 'make backup → age-encrypt → off-host; restore drill.'

Below the steps, a quiet line (var(--text-dim) 14px): 'Full script: download/demo-script.md'.
Footer micro: '08 / 11'.
Speaker notes: Keep the demo honest — show the operability layer, not just the chat UI; the DR drill is the most persuasive beat.

slides.title: Honest limitations
slides.task_brief:
HONEST LIMITATIONS SLIDE — this slide builds credibility. Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'WHAT IS HONESTLY NOT DONE'. H1 (Space Grotesk 40px, var(--text)) 'An operability claim is only credible if you know the gaps.'

Below, a vertical list of 6 limitation rows, each a .card-elev row (~80px tall, full width). Each row has: a status chip on the left (rounded pill) — either 'EVALUATED' (var(--text-mute) bg) or 'OPEN' (var(--warn) text on var(--bg-card)) — then the limitation title (Space Grotesk 18px) and a one-line explanation (Inter 14px, var(--text-dim)) on the right; ADR reference in monospace at the far right.

1. chip 'EVALUATED' — 'Single host, no HA' — 'Everything on one VPS; deliberate (ADR-0001). ADR-0015 documents multi-host.' — 'ADR-0015'
2. chip 'OPEN' — 'No automated rotation schedule' — 'rotate-secrets.sh exists & tested; scheduling is manual.' — 'ADR-0013'
3. chip 'EVALUATED' — 'cosign verify at deploy time' — 'Verified in CI; deploy.sh does not re-verify before switch. Deferred on cost.' — 'ADR-0025'
4. chip 'EVALUATED' — 'Business-endpoint load tests' — 'k6 covers /health/live/ only; RAG queries need the app.' — 'ADR-0018'
5. chip 'OPEN' — 'Terraform provider-specific' — 'Ships for Hetzner; swapping providers needs a block change.' — 'ADR-0028'
6. chip 'OPEN' — 'promtail metrics stage' — 'Latency/5xx SLIs declared; metrics stage does not yet emit. Pipeline architecture verified end-to-end.' — 'ADR-0035'

Footer micro: '09 / 11'.
Speaker notes: The last row is the important one — the SLIs are declared and alerts load, but the underlying promtail metrics stage is open work; documented in ADR-0035, not hidden; the drill runs every push and goes green when fixed.

slides.title: Maturity at a glance
slides.task_brief:
MATURITY SLIDE. Top eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim)) 'MATURITY MODEL'. H1 (Space Grotesk 40px, var(--text)) '13 of 15 capabilities shipped. 2 evaluated.'

Main content: a row of FOUR big stat cards (each .card, ~280×220px), each with a huge JetBrains Mono number (56px) in var(--accent), a label (Space Grotesk 16px, var(--text)) below, and a one-line proof (Inter 13px, var(--text-dim)) under that:
1. '13' — 'shipped' — 'zero-downtime deploy, backups, DR, observability, SLOs, supply chain, TLS, rotation, load test, chaos, IaC, maintenance, capacity, audit trail'
2. '2' — 'evaluated / planned' — 'multi-host HA (ADR-0015), business load tests'
3. '27' — 'CI workflows' — 'run on every push'
4. '29' — 'ADRs' — 'every decision recorded'

Below the stat row, a horizontal progress bar (rounded, var(--bg-elev) track, var(--ok) fill ~87% wide) with a label '87% of capabilities shipped (13/15)' in monospace above it.
Footer micro: '10 / 11 · v1.1.4'.
Speaker notes: The point is not the number — it is that each shipped capability has a CI drill as proof, and each gap is an ADR, not a surprise.

slides.title: Closing — the difference
slides.task_brief:
CLOSING SLIDE. Dark background with .grid-bg overlay. Centered content block.
Eyebrow (monospace, var(--text-dim), uppercase): 'THE DIFFERENCE'.
Main statement (Space Grotesk 40px, var(--text), max-width ~1000px, centered): 'A docker-compose file is not a product you can run. StackSmith is.'
Below it, a single line (Inter 18px, var(--text-dim), centered): 'Backups, SLOs, disaster recovery, supply-chain signing, runbooks — shipped, proven in CI, honest about what is not done.'

Below that, a centered row of three monospace contact chips (each .card small): 'github.com/Abolfazlrwm/stacksmith' (with Material Icon 'code'), 'release v1.1.4' (icon 'tag'), 'MIT licensed' (icon 'gavel').

At the very bottom, centered, small monospace (var(--text-mute)): 'Thank you.   ·   Questions?'
Footer micro: '11 / 11'.
No photos. Generous whitespace; the closing should feel quiet and confident, not busy.
Speaker notes: End on the one-line thesis; invite questions; have demo-script.md and product-overview.md ready to share.
